correctness.rationale: Read the exact local pairwise definition eta(epsilon)=dist(f^{-1}(1), B\U(x,epsilon)); the closed outside-distance constraint matters. The hyperplane distance from (t,y) equals 1-t, attained at (1,y). For finite p, for fixed t the maximum distance to x is [(1-t)^p+1-|t|^p]^(1/p), attained with y of norm (1-|t|^p)^(1/p). This envelope is nonincreasing in t and for slice depth d has sharp radius G_p(d)^(1/p), G_p(d)=d^p+1-|1-d|^p. At p=1, G=2min(d,1) and eta=epsilon/2. At p>1 finite G is strictly increasing 0..2^p, giving inverse eta=G_p^{-1}(epsilon^p). At p=infinity the sharp radius is max(1,d), yielding eta=0 through epsilon=1 and eta=epsilon above; exact witnesses use any unit u in nonzero Y. G_p(1/2)=1 gives finite-p pivot; G_p(d)=p d+o(d) gives eta~epsilon^p/p. All endpoints and nonreflexive Y allowed; saved rational/sampled verify.py is only a consistency check.
residual_risks: Index is local at (x,f), not global across all support pairs; p=infinity radius at d=0 is nonzero because the exposing functional fails to strongly expose x.
